history.prompt: Clean isometric cutaway illustration, technical drawing style, axonometric projection. A central network routing hub module glowing with a deep red malfunction light, connected via heavy rigid conduits to five peripheral server rack modules that sit completely dark and unpowered. Flat muted slate palette with deep red as the single accent color, thin consistent line weight, recognizable rack hardware and cooling pipes with visible depth, unlabelled, generous empty margin.

style_when: the news is structural and abstract — a stack reordered, a layer added, a flow rerouted — and there is no literal object that carries it, so the idea is stated as a small physical assembly of recognisable parts rather than as bare shapes
prompt: Matte clay 3D render of a small mechanical network assembly resting on a weathered brushed steel surface. Three distinct server blade housings are connected by thick physical routing cables into one central, unified control module. The central module acts as a structural bottleneck in the arrangement. Matte muted teal and slate grey palette. Visible moulding seams and soft contact shadows. One directional key light raking across the assembly from the left, casting deep shadows into the generous empty right margin. Asymmetric composition, no text.
negative_prompt: text, letters, numbers, wordmarks, signage, UI, watermark, logo
rationale: The story describes an abstract architectural flaw in network routing rather than a single photographable event. A matte clay render distills this systemic flaw into a clean, tangible mechanical assembly, illustrating the convergence into a single vulnerability without unnecessary visual noise.
subject: multiple server blade housings routing into one centralized control module
alt_text: Three server blade housings routing cables into one central matte clay control module on brushed steel.
caption: When multiple cloud regions share a single network gateway, the primary benefit of distributed redundancy is lost.
title: Cloud Shared Control Plane Architecture
